Where We Are

Part III connects stored data to models, retrieval, and actions

Outline: ML Systems

01 · From Data to Predictions

§ Data and Features

Data Scientist and ML EngineerA model needs a reliable path from source data to predictions

Roles span data preparation, training, and serving

ML PipelineTraining transforms prepared examples into an evaluated model

Features, training, and evaluation form one pipeline

Training and InferenceInference applies the learned model to new inputs

Training uses labels; inference receives new inputs

ML Pipeline at ScaleFeature, training, and inference pipelines can run independently

Shared stores connect pipelines with different schedules

ML InfrastructureOperational data feeds analytical stores and ML pipelines

ML systems connect operational and analytical data

Feature PipelineA feature pipeline creates model inputs from source records

Feature computation precedes both training and serving

Recap: Data PreparationModel features depend on the same collection and preparation decisions

Raw sources become structured tables before features

Feature StoreA feature store manages reusable feature values and definitions

A shared feature store feeds training and inference

Feature TablesEntity keys connect features from different source tables

Joins align transaction, user, and credit features

Training TableA training example combines features with a target label

One row contains the features available for one prediction

Feature Update FrequenciesDifferent feature groups can refresh at different rates

A recent transaction and a user profile age differently

Windowed FeaturesAggregations summarize events over a defined time window

The aggregation window is part of the feature definition

Point-in-Time CorrectnessReconstruct inputs using what the system knew at prediction time

Use a record only if it was available at 10:00

Recap: Feature AvailabilityA late report existed in event time but was unavailable at prediction time

FeatureEventAvailableValue
temperature09:5509:5631
alarm_count09:5810:123
vibration09:5009:510.8
A late report existed in event time but was unavailable at prediction time

Demo: Point-in-Time FeaturesCompare event-time filtering with availability-time filtering

  1. Join Predictions and Features using machine_id; filter event_at ≤ predicted_at.
  2. Also filter available_at ≤ predicted_at. Which feature disappears?
Ctrl/⌘ + Enter

Answer: Point-in-Time FeaturesUse only features that were available when the prediction was made

SELECT p.id, f.feature, f.value
FROM Predictions p JOIN Features f ON f.machine_id=p.machine_id
WHERE f.event_at <= p.predicted_at AND f.available_at <= p.predicted_at
ORDER BY p.id, f.feature;
The late alarm report is excluded

Caveat: Training–Serving SkewDifferent feature code can change the meaning of an input

Same feature name, different computation

§ Training and Serving

Training PipelineA training pipeline reads versioned examples and produces an artifact

The model artifact leaves the training pipeline

Train, Validation, and TestUse validation for choices and reserve test data for final evaluation

The original 70/15/15 split is an example, not a rule

Training IterationRepeated experiments consume the same controlled evaluation protocol

Training and validation guide the iteration

Experiment RecordRecord the inputs that produced each candidate model

The record names every input that built the model

Experiment CycleTry, evaluate, and revise before promoting a candidate

Iteration changes the candidate, not the held-out test

Batch InferenceBatch inference scores a collection of records on a schedule

Features enter a model and predictions return to storage

Online InferenceOnline inference answers an individual request within a latency budget

A request joins current features with the deployed model

Real-Time ML SystemLow-latency features and model serving are separate components

Feature freshness and response latency are different requirements

Model Serving ComponentsA transformer and predictor can share a serving endpoint

Transformation and prediction remain observable stages

02 · Building and Releasing Models

§ Development

MLOpsMLOps coordinates development, deployment, and monitoring of ML systems

The deployed system returns observations to development

Changing ML ProductsData and targets can change after deployment

The world keeps changing after the release test

Release AutomationAutomation connects repeatable tests to controlled releases

Every change passes the same tests and baseline comparison

DevOpsDevOps automates the software build, test, and release lifecycle

Versioned code enters a tested release pipeline

DevOps and MLOpsData and model changes can trigger ML validation and retraining

ML pipelines respond to more than code commits

Reproducible MLReproduction needs more than a saved model

Code → Data → Training → Artifact

Model DevelopmentTrain and test on separate data before deployment

A candidate passes a test before the serving pipeline

Development EnvironmentsDevelopment and production require explicit artifact promotion

Move versioned artifacts across environment boundaries

Reproducibility DependenciesCode, feature groups, and training data form a dependency graph

A model version points back to its inputs

Versioned ML AssetsChoose a versioning mechanism for each asset

AssetVersion keyReproduction input
CodeGit commitCode + environment
FeaturesDefinition + schemaTransformation + snapshot
Training dataSnapshot IDRows + split
ModelArtifact IDParameters + dependencies
Choose a versioning mechanism for each asset

Schema VersioningA renamed or retyped feature can break a deployed model

A pinned schema version keeps the deployed model working

Data VersioningLarge datasets need versioned references and reproducible reads

MechanismStoresUse
GitCode / small metadataTrack definitions
DVC-style trackingPointers + object storageTrack external files
Table snapshotsVersioned table stateReproduce a query
Large datasets need versioned references and reproducible reads

Versioned TablesA table snapshot can reproduce historical training inputs

Versioned reads connect a training run to a data snapshot

§ Validation

ML Test LayersEach stage needs a test for its own failure modes

Each stage gets a test for its own failure

Tests in ML SystemsValidation follows the dependencies from data to serving

Tests attach to the stage that owns the failure

Data and Model TestsTest contracts and quality with different assertions

TestExample assertion
Schemamachine_id exists; temperature is numeric
Data qualityMissing temperatures below a chosen threshold
Feature correctnessFeature available_at ≤ prediction time
Model qualityRecall on rare failures meets the release criterion
Test contracts and quality with different assertions

Infrastructure and Monitoring TestsTest the pipeline as well as its output

LayerExample
IntegrationA source batch reaches the scored table
ReproducibilityThe recorded snapshot reproduces the feature rows
RollbackThe previous model version can be restored
MonitoringA missing-label spike raises an alert
Test the pipeline as well as its output

Testable Feature FunctionsSeparate transformation logic from storage and orchestration

Feature logic lives in modules that tests import

03 · Monitoring Models in Use

§ Observability

Prediction LogsLink each prediction to the model and feature versions

One log row links request, inputs, model and outcome

Feature and Prediction LogsLogged inputs support debugging and later evaluation

Logs link input features, model versions, and outcomes

Delayed LabelsPrediction quality becomes visible only when outcomes arrive

Recent predictions have no outcome yet

§ Drift and Updates

Case study: Data DriftDifferent drift locations call for different investigations

Feature-pipeline, serving, label, and concept drift differ

Drift TypesDistribution change and predictive relationship change are distinct

Inputs, labels, or the relationship can move

Population Stability IndexPSI compares binned feature frequencies across two periods

PSI sums the change in each bin

Caveat: Drift and QualityAn input shift is a reason to investigate, not an automatic retraining order

Input shift and quality loss are separate questions

Controlled Model UpdateValidate a candidate before it replaces the serving model

Investigate → Train → Evaluate → Release

Takeaway: Operate the data behind the model

1Reuse the same feature definitions in training and serving
2Version and test data, code, and models together
3Measure drift, validate quality, and control updates
